lead.text: France's tax authority admits attackers stole income, family-quotient and withholding data on 678,000 people and businesses
A suspected China-nexus actor is exploiting a critical VMware vCenter flaw across 361 hosts in 47 countries, deploying a Babuk-derived encryptor
Clop's Windchill victim list keeps growing — Philips and GE are now confirmed investigating alongside Shell, with Reuters counting nearly 50 named companies
A new Mirai-derived botnet, Evooo1Bot, is turning routers and IoT gear into DDoS launchpads and SOCKS5 proxy relays
New AmnesiaStealer malware clones victims' authenticated Chromium browser sessions for live remote control on macOS
Microsoft assigns a CVE to the unpatched Defender "ShieldBreak" zero-day and confirms it's building a fix — none exists yet

items.headline: French tax authority data breach affects 678,000 individuals
items.summary: Attackers used stolen credentials from a DGFiP employee and an authorized third party during June–July intrusions; a threat actor going by "ZeroBytes" listed the stolen database for sale on a hacking forum August 12. Exposed data covers taxable income, family-quotient and withholding-tax rates for individuals plus SIREN and cadastral records for businesses — account logins were not compromised.
items.why: Tax and property data at this scale is prime fuel for targeted phishing against millions of French taxpayers — watch for official DGFiP letters starting next week, and treat unsolicited "tax data" emails or calls as suspect.

items.headline: Suspected China-Nexus Actor Exploits VMware vCenter Flaw, Deploys Babuk-Derived Ransomware
items.summary: German incident-response firm QUIRSO found 361 compromised vCenter IPs across 47 countries; systems began contacting attacker infrastructure August 3, just five days after Broadcom's July 29 patch for CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8), a directory-traversal RCE. Attackers used reverse SSH for persistence and dropped a Babuk-derived encryptor.
items.why: Any vCenter host that wasn't patched within days of disclosure should be treated as likely already compromised — hunt for reverse_ssh and rogue cron jobs, not just patch and move on.

items.headline: Philips and GE investigating Clop ransomware data theft claims
items.summary: What's new:Since Friday's report that only Shell was investigating an 89GB claim, Clop has now confirmed targeting Philips (13.5GB, a contained enterprise-server compromise) and GE as part of the same PTC Windchill/FlexPLM zero-day campaign — Reuters now counts nearly 50 named victim companies in total, including Fiserv.
items.why: The victim list is still growing a week after disclosure — any organization running internet-exposed Windchill or FlexPLM should already have patched CVE-2026-12569 and hunted for the campaign's JSP webshells.

items.headline: New Evooo1Bot Linux botnet turns routers into traffic-relay nodes
items.summary: Built on Mirai's DDoS engine, Evooo1Bot adds 16 flooding methods, encrypted C2, an SSH brute-forcer, a credential sniffer and an exploit dispatcher targeting known flaws in D-Link, Tenda, Hikvision, Zyxel and TP-Link gear, turning compromised edge devices into SOCKS5 proxy relays.
items.why: Internet-facing routers and IoT/edge devices from the named vendors need patching and default-credential rotation now, before they're absorbed into this botnet's proxy network.

items.headline: New AmnesiaStealer macOS malware hijacks browser sessions via remote control
items.summary: Distributed via ClickFix pages spoofing a GitHub download, the Rust-based stealer harvests credentials, crypto wallets, Apple Notes and Keychain data across 16 Chromium browsers, then clones the victim's authenticated browser profile into a hidden headless instance the attacker can drive live.
items.why: The "copy-paste this Terminal command" ClickFix lure keeps working on Mac users — train staff to never paste unknown commands into Terminal, regardless of how legitimate the download page looks.

items.headline: Microsoft working on Defender patch for ShieldBreak zero-day
items.summary: What's new:Microsoft has now assigned CVE-2026-69414 to the ShieldBreak Defender-patch-bypass covered here Aug 12 and publicly confirmed it's developing a fix. As of this morning no patch is available, and Microsoft's advisory rates exploitation "more likely."
items.why: A CVE number makes the flaw trackable in vulnerability-management tooling, but there's still no fix — keep monitoring for Cloud Filter API (cfapi) callback abuse until Microsoft ships one.

items.headline: Max severity SAP Commerce Cloud flaw now targeted in attacks
items.summary: CVE-2026-58231, an unauthenticated RCE in the Data Hub Adapter, requires no privileges and no working public PoC — yet Field Effect and Defused detected exploitation attempts within three days of the patch, suggesting attackers reverse-engineered SAP's fix.
items.why: Upgrade to SAP Commerce Cloud 2211.55 or 2211-jdk21.17 now — low-complexity, unauthenticated RCE at CVSS 10.0 is about as bad as it gets.

items.headline: Lazarus hackers exploited Windows zero-day to target defense firms
items.summary: North Korea's Lazarus group used fake Lockheed Martin job-offer lures to chain a use-after-free in afd.sys (CVE-2026-68820) into SYSTEM privileges and deploy its FudModule kernel rootkit against European and Indian defense contractors for roughly five weeks before Check Point's report led Microsoft to patch it on August 11's Patch Tuesday.
items.why: Defense-sector staff should treat unsolicited recruiter PDFs as a credible initial-access vector — Lazarus has now paired that lure with a kernel zero-day, not just credential phishing.

items.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google API Flaw Let Weaker AI Models Decode Stronger Models' Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers found all three providers encrypt hidden reasoning blocks with one key shared globally across sessions and users; replaying a block into a weaker model from the same provider family made it transcribe the hidden reasoning in plaintext, letting the team recover 182 real credentials from 315,320 decoded blocks found in public GitHub and Hugging Face agent-trajectory logs.
items.why: Treat any published "agent trajectory" or reasoning log as potentially containing recoverable secrets — audit what your own agents expose before sharing logs publicly.

items.headline: Local AI Security Fragility: Vulnerabilities Inside the Engine Running Your Local Models
items.summary: Cyera Research Labs found 10 vulnerabilities — use-after-free, integer overflow and out-of-bounds flaws — in llama.cpp, the inference engine underlying Ollama, LM Studio, Jan and GPT4All. Two llama-server bugs rated CVSS 9.2 remain unpatched, exposing any organization running local AI inference to untrusted traffic.
items.why: Nearly every popular "run AI locally" tool inherits these flaws — restrict network exposure of local inference servers until patches land.

items.headline: A10 Networks introduces AI Gateway to secure and manage enterprise AI
items.summary: Unveiled at Black Hat USA 2026, the A10 AI Gateway is a centralized control plane routing and governing traffic across every AI agent, application and LLM an organization uses, applying access policies by user/group and tracking per-request cost, deployable on-prem, in private cloud, or air-gapped.
items.why: Enterprises struggling to inventory "shadow AI" agents now have another chokepoint option for centralizing visibility — worth evaluating against existing API gateway and CASB tooling before adding a new control plane.

items.headline: Searchlight Cyber combines exposure and threat intelligence in new PTEM platform
items.summary: Searchlight unified its Assetnote attack-surface tool (now "Searchlight Exposure") with its Cerberus/DarkIQ dark-web monitoring (now "Searchlight Threat") into a single Preemptive Threat Exposure Management platform aimed at shrinking the gap between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation.
items.why: As AI compresses exploit-development timelines from months to hours, exposure-management platforms that fuse attacker intelligence with asset visibility are becoming table stakes rather than a nice-to-have.

items.headline: xAI ships Grok 4.6, tying GPT-5.6 Sol for third on Artificial Analysis
items.summary: xAI released Grok 4.6, a post-training refresh of Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic work that scored 61 on Artificial Analysis's index — level with GPT-5.6 Sol and ahead of Kimi K3 — while pricing at $2/$6 per million input/output tokens.
items.why: xAI is now trading blows with OpenAI at roughly half the price, keeping the frontier a four-lab race even as the marquee US labs stay quiet this week.

items.headline: ByteDance opens up Seed 2.1 Turbo, a faster, cheaper coding-agent variant
items.summary: ByteDance widened access to Seed 2.1 Turbo, a multimodal 262K-context model aimed at high-frequency coding and long-horizon agent workflows — the lower-cost sibling to the flagship Seed 2.1 Pro that powers its Doubao assistant.
items.why: Another Chinese lab pushing an inexpensive, agent-tuned model deepens the pricing pressure US enterprises are already using to justify multi-model stacks.

items.headline: An unreleased Claude pushes a 37-year-old Riemann-zeta bound from 41.6% to 67.2%
items.summary: Anthropic disclosed that a research build of Claude improved a proven lower bound tied to the Riemann Hypothesis over two Claude Code sessions, 60 sub-agents, and 31M tokens. It did not prove the hypothesis, but the machine-verified result — reviewed by external mathematicians — is the biggest single advance on that specific bound in decades.
items.why: It is a concrete data point that frontier models can now synthesize scattered specialist literature into genuinely new, checkable math rather than just restating known results.

items.headline: State of Open Models: open weights are closing on the frontier
items.summary: Hugging Face's summer landscape review finds open-weight models — led by Chinese releases like Kimi K3, Qwen, DeepSeek and GLM — now trailing the best closed models by a narrowing margin on coding, reasoning and agent benchmarks, even as several labs quietly hold weights back for safety review.
items.why: The open/closed capability gap is now measured in weeks, reshaping how enterprises weigh cost, control and data residency against raw frontier performance.

items.headline: ChatGPT for Mac adds "Computer History" — a searchable log of what you did
items.summary: OpenAI's opt-in Computer History feature turns clicks, typing, shortcuts and app-switches on a Mac into searchable "memories" so ChatGPT can recall the last file you edited or summarize your morning. Unlike Microsoft Recall it skips screenshots, but critics flag that it records keystroke-level activity.
items.why: Persistent, assistant-readable activity histories make AI far more useful — and turn collection, retention and deletion controls into a new layer of OS-level privacy risk.

items.headline: Wispr Flow raises $280M at a $2B valuation and pushes past dictation
items.summary: Voice-AI startup Wispr nearly tripled its valuation to $2B in nine months, with revenue up more than 150% for four straight quarters. The Menlo-led round funds a move beyond speech-to-text toward hands-free AI work across apps.
items.why: Voice is becoming a serious primary interface for AI work, and investors are paying application-layer premiums for tools showing real enterprise traction.

items.headline: DoiT buys AI-spend startup Attribute to track cost across tokens, models and agents
items.summary: Cloud-optimization firm DoiT acquired Israeli startup Attribute — which gives a real-time view of spending across AI tokens, models, agents and customers — in a deal estimated near $65M. DoiT expects customers' monthly AI spend to triple within a year while few can calculate AI ROI.
items.why: As agentic workloads scale, "FinOps for AI" — knowing which model or agent is burning money — is becoming essential enterprise plumbing.

items.headline: Stripe clinches a >$7B deal to acquire model-router OpenRouter
items.summary: Payments giant Stripe agreed to buy OpenRouter — a gateway that routes developer requests across 400+ AI models by price and performance — for more than $7B, roughly a 5x markup on the $1.3B valuation it raised at in May. Stripe declined to confirm, so treat it as reported.
items.why: A multibillion-dollar price validates neutral model-routing as core AI infrastructure — and plants Stripe between developers and every major model provider.

items.headline: Nvidia nears a ~$105B credit guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio campus
items.summary: What's new since last week's report that Nvidia was trimming its backstop below $120B: the two are now said to be nearing a signed deal, with Nvidia guaranteeing roughly $105B for the first phase of the 10-GW Pike County build and separately weighing a ~$3B investment in SB Energy to help power it.
items.why: Nvidia is increasingly the financier of the AI buildout it also supplies — a circular arrangement investors are watching for concentration risk.

items.headline: Higgsfield raises $400M at a $5.4B valuation as AI video goes enterprise
items.summary: The two-year-old AI video and image startup more than quadrupled its valuation, with annualized revenue climbing from ~$20M a year ago to $700M. Founder Alex Mashrabov says businesses now drive most revenue, up from under a quarter in January.
items.why: AI-generated video is shifting from creator novelty to a real enterprise-content category — and investors are still writing big checks for fast-growing AI applications, not just foundation labs.

items.headline: Anthropic is on track for its first profitable quarter
items.summary: Anthropic is projected to post an operating profit around $559M on Q2 revenue of $10.9B — more than double Q1 — a milestone that arrives roughly two years ahead of the 2028 timeline it showed investors last year. It remains deeply unprofitable on a cumulative basis.
items.why: A frontier lab flipping a quarter into the black — as OpenAI still burns ~$14B this year — sharpens the contrast between the two leaders' strategies ahead of both firms' expected IPOs.

items.headline: Unitree sets an Aug 19 Shanghai IPO after record retail demand
items.summary: China's Unitree — already the world's largest humanoid-robot maker by sales — is set to begin trading on Shanghai's STAR Market on Aug 19 at a ~$9B valuation, becoming the mainland's first general-purpose robotics listing after an IPO that was thousands of times oversubscribed.
items.why: It is the first public-market test of humanoid robotics as an operating business, as AI money rotates from software into "physical AI."

items.headline: OpenAI disbands its Preparedness team, folding frontier-risk work into product groups
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly dissolved the team that assessed whether its models could enable catastrophic bio or cyber misuse, distributing that work into specialized divisions. It follows the earlier wind-downs of its superalignment and AGI-readiness teams and several senior safety departures, as the company preps for a public listing.
items.why: How labs govern frontier risk — a dedicated watchdog versus embedded ownership — is becoming as scrutinized by regulators as raw benchmarks.

items.headline: Stripe to acquire AI "gateway" OpenRouter for more than $7 billion
items.summary: Bloomberg reports payments giant Stripe has finalized a deal to buy OpenRouter — the marketplace that routes requests across 400+ AI models for 8 million users — for over $7 billion, roughly five times the startup's $1.3B valuation from May.
items.why: Model-routing and cost optimization have become core enterprise-AI plumbing, and the deal pushes Stripe well beyond payments into the AI infrastructure stack.

items.headline: Nvidia's $5B Intel bet is now worth ~$30B; filing reveals a $21B SpaceX stake and a full Arm exit
items.summary: Nvidia's latest 13F shows its ~214.8M-share Intel position (bought at $23.28) has ballooned to about $30B, alongside a newly disclosed $21B stake in SpaceX and a complete sell-off of its Arm holdings.
items.why: Nvidia is increasingly acting as a strategic investor shaping the chip and space supply chains its own business depends on.

items.headline: Waymo wins California approval to expand robotaxis across 18 counties
items.summary: After nearly seven months of review, the CPUC cleared Waymo to charge for fully driverless rides across most of California's population — all of the Bay Area and Los Angeles, plus new Sacramento and San Diego markets.
items.why: Cements Waymo's commercial-autonomy lead while Tesla's "Robotaxi" still runs with human safety drivers under a limo-style permit.

items.headline: Tech layoffs in 2026 have already surpassed all of 2025
items.summary: With fresh cuts at Google, TikTok, Etsy and Zillow, 2026 tech layoffs passed roughly 125,000 by early August — beating 2025's full-year total with four months to spare, per layoffs.fyi.
items.why: The pace, driven by AI-capex reallocation and automation, points to a structural reset in how tech companies staff.

items.headline: Google unveils the Pixel 11 lineup, including the Pixel 11 Pro Fold
items.summary: At Made by Google, the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL and Pro Fold debuted on the new Tensor G6 with a redesigned glass camera bar, a "HiLight" notification LED, 3,600-nit Pro screens and Gemini-centric camera features; the base model starts at $899 and ships Aug 20.
items.why: Google's most "Gemini-first" phones yet reframe Android as an "intelligence system" — and raise prices across the flagship line.

items.headline: Tesla adds 2.4 kW vehicle-to-load power to the Model Y with an $80 adapter
items.summary: A new $80 adapter unlocks 2.4 kW of vehicle-to-load output on the Model Y Premium, letting owners run tools or appliances directly off the car's battery.
items.why: A small but practical step toward bidirectional power that turns EVs into mobile backup batteries.

items.headline: Ferrari's first EV, the Luce, sells for $40 million at auction
items.summary: Chassis 0 of Ferrari's first electric car, the Luce, fetched about $40 million — roughly 36x its estimate — as the marque's initial EV run sold out immediately.
items.why: A striking signal that even legacy performance brands and their collectors are now betting on electric.

items.headline: Cloudflare logs 13 outages in 8 days as R2 storage falters
items.summary: Cloudflare's status page recorded 13 separate incidents between Aug 7 and Aug 14 — spanning R2 object storage, Durable Objects, Workers KV/AI and email security — none as large as its November 2025 global outage, but striking for their frequency.
items.why: The streak revives hard questions about concentration risk when one vendor sits in front of roughly a fifth of web traffic.

items.headline: "Ted Lasso" season 4 is Apple TV's biggest launch ever
items.summary: The show's fourth-season premiere drew nearly 300 million minutes of viewing in just two days, the largest debut in Apple TV history as Apple leans on tentpole originals.
items.why: Reinforces streaming's central role in Apple's fast-growing services business and its push for franchise-scale hits.

items.headline: SpaceX sets a record with two Falcon 9 launches just 38.5 minutes apart
items.summary: SpaceX launched Globalstar satellites from Florida and the classified USSF-366 payload from California only 38.5 minutes apart, and logged its 650th Falcon booster landing in the process.
items.why: The cadence shows orbital launch becoming routine industrial infrastructure across both US coasts.

items.headline: A black hole shreds a "super sun" in the most powerful stellar blast yet seen
items.summary: The tidal-disruption event nicknamed "the Whippet" (AT2024wpp) briefly shone as bright as 400 billion suns; new analysis of fast-moving helium suggests part of the doomed star may have survived.
items.why: Pushes the known limits of these rare, ultra-luminous events and how supermassive black holes devour stars.

items.headline: SpaceX targets its first Starship "ship" tower-catch on Flight 14, as soon as late August
items.summary: SpaceX plans to attempt its first catch of the Starship upper stage with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms and to deploy operational Starlink V3 satellites on Flight 14, pending FAA approval.
items.why: Catching the ship would be a major reusability milestone with direct implications for Starlink and NASA's Artemis lunar lander.
